transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-12-01
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Rajiv Menon (Redwood SE), Maya Huang (Redwood Product); Tom Ellis, Priya Kapoor, Diego Ramos (Skyward)

Summary: short sync to align on marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture for a joint solution, and staging + rollout plan. Agreed action items and timeline.

[00:00] Lena: hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is lena from Redwood, and we have rajiv and maya with me. thanks for making time.
[00:10] Tom: yeah thanks, this is tom at Skyward, we wanted to make sure we align on the marketplace listing requirements and the reference architecture, and also verify the private deployment patterns.
[00:25] Rajiv: cool, quick agenda — listing checklist, reference arch for a redwood-backed inference integration, auth and tenant model, staging tests, and next steps. is that okay?
[00:35] Priya: yes, that's great. quick note, our primary constraint is data residency and we need KMS integration for customer keys. also, we prefer to route inference via our api gateway.
[00:50] Rajiv: got it. so we usually support multiple integration modes: hosted API (Redwood hosted), dedicated/reserved capacity, and private VPC/on-prem. for marketplace listing we typically highlight which modes are supported.
[01:10] Diego: for the marketplace we want a single tile that supports both hosted and private options, is that feasible?
[01:20] Maya: yeah that's doable; we can document the variants. we should call out network requirements, egress rules, and certs for mTLS if using private.
[01:35] Tom: on the private side, do you have a sample reference arch for a VPC deployment? we need to show how our customers can connect to redwood via peering or private link.
[01:50] Rajiv: we do — i'll send an updated ref arch. just to flag, sometimes our docs call it Redwood Private or Redwood OnPrem, and the transcription in older notes shows 'Redwood Dedicaed' so sorry for the typos. but the architecture covers VPC peering, PrivateLink, and optional on-prem appliance.
[02:10] Priya: perfect. can you also include recommended instance types, gpu counts, and quantization guidance? our customers will want to estimate cost.
[02:25] Rajiv: yes, we'll include perf profiles — per-token latency numbers, throughput at batch sizes, and recommended GPU families. we'll also show KV cache and batching options, and notes on compiler/kernels.
[02:40] Tom: any pitfalls for marketplace listings? like compliance or screenshots?
[02:50] Lena: typically the marketplace requires a short description, icon/screenshots, a deployment template (cloudformation/helm), and security docs: SOC2, ISO, audit logs. for Partner Marketplace we also include a tested quickstart and list of supported regions.
[03:10] Diego: does Redwood maintain audit log hooks we can surface in our docs?
[03:20] Rajiv: yes, there's built-in audit logging and we can show where logs land and how to forward to a customer's SIEM — we support syslog, CloudWatch, GCS sinks, etc.
[03:35] Priya: KMS integration — do you support customer-managed keys and HSM?
[03:40] Maya: yes, KMS + HSM integrations are supported in Private mode; for Hosted mode we have encryption at rest and optional bring-your-own-key via supported cloud kms. we'll attach the security whitepaper.
[03:55] Tom: great. on marketplace compliance do we need a separate contract or can we list under the existing partner agreement?
[04:05] Lena: usually marketplace listings require a partner agreement appendix; i can coordinate legal but for now we'll move on tech items. legal will reach out if needed.
[04:20] [05:00] Rajiv: we also discussed the integration points: 1) Deployment templates — helm chart and infra module, 2) API contract — endpoints and auth, 3) Observability hooks — metrics/trace/logging, and 4) Reference app for quick verification.
[05:30] Tom: about auth — we want to use our API gateway issuing JWTs to Redwood, is that supported?
[05:40] Rajiv: yes, JWT bearer tokens are supported; for private we can do mTLS or mutual TLS; SAML/SSO is supported for console access.
[05:55] Priya: what's the recommended flow for a customer that wants to use Skyward's marketplace tile to deploy Redwood-backed inference?
[06:05] Maya: recommend flow: customer clicks tile -> provisioned stack (helm + infra) -> Redwood tenant created or linked -> keys configured (customer KMS if private) -> run sample workload. We'll add a diagram to the ref arch.
[06:30] Tom: staging — we need a staging tenant for integration tests. can you provision one for us?
[06:40] Lena: yes we can, tom. rajiv, can you own creating a staging tenant and share keys?
[06:46] Rajiv: yep i'll provision a host and share credentials in a secure vault.
[06:50] [15:00] Priya: any specific network ports or egress rules we should call out?
[15:10] Rajiv: typically 443 outbound for API calls, and grpc over TLS for high-throughput paths. if using private link, then you'll have private IPs only. we'll include a matrix for network requirements.
[15:30] Diego: what about the listing screenshots — what format do you want?
[15:35] Maya: PNGs, 1200x600 for the hero, and two smaller 800x400 screenshots. also include a short 30 second demo video. i'll draft the copy.
[16:00] Tom: i saw references to 'KV cache' and 'batching' in your docs; can you summarize how batching affects latency and cost?
[16:10] Rajiv: sure — batching increases throughput and reduces per-token cost but can add queuing latency. we recommend hybrid batching with tight latency SLOs and prefix caching to speed up repeated prompts. we'll include perf curves.
[16:30] Priya: for private deployments can customers bring custom quantized models?
[16:40] Rajiv: yes, we support shipping custom model artifacts for private and dedicated; we have a model onboarding checklist including quantization profile and kernel compatibility notes.
[16:55] Lena: quick note: we should confirm marketplace compliance items; maya will send the listing copy and screenshots by monday.
[17:05] Maya: yes i'll share a draft in the partner drive and link in slack. link: https://redwood.example.com/partner-drive/skyward-marketplace
[17:20] Diego: for the rollout test can we plan a smoke test that runs sample inference with 1k tokens?
[17:28] Rajiv: yes, we'll run a throughput smoke test and a latency SLO test. propose 2026-12-15 for the joint run.
[17:40] Priya: anything else on legal or billing?
[17:45] Lena: billing for marketplace sales can be through the marketplace or via direct billing; we can support both. we'll follow up with finance.
[18:00] Tom: thanks, this was helpful.
[18:05] Lena: recap of next steps — we will send checklist, ref arch, and quickstart; Skyward will provide staging and keys; schedule test on the 15th.
[18:20] Diego: thanks all, talk soon.

Action items (captured in metadata): Lena to share listing checklist; Rajiv to provision staging and prepare helm values; Maya to draft screenshots and copy; Tom to provision tenant and keys.

References & artifacts mentioned: marketplace checklist deck (link: https://redwood.example.com/docs/marketplace-checklist), reference architecture PDF (link: /redwood/ref-archs/skyward-redwood-vpc.pdf), quickstart helm chart (repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/marketplace-quickstart).
